template.name: Mindray BeneFusion eSP Vet Syringe Pump
template.desc: Mindray BeneFusion eSP veterinary syringe pump. Class I, internally powered, IP33; the applied part is the syringe, marked defibrillation-proof type CF but non-metallic with no electrical connection, so there are no applied-part leakage tests (service manual H-046-021904-00 v2.0 Appendix A, p. A-6; ops manual H-046-021887-00 v5.0 A.1 and 2.2). From the CHS Ansur template “0000-Benefusion eSP 000000000 Vet EST+PVT AS-NZS 3551 DD.MM.YYYY.mtt”. Electrical safety to AS/NZS 3551:2012+A2. Changed from Ansur: earth leakage NC 5000, ON 10000 µA (B11.6) (Ansur: NC 500, ON 1000 µA); enclosure leakage NC 100, ON 500, OE 500 µA (Ansur: NC 100, ON -500, OE 500 µA); protective earth resistance ≤ 0.2 Ω added (Ansur had none; the manual gives < 0.2 Ω, A.2). Changed from Ansur: accuracy tests use the manual’s VTBI and rate per syringe (service manual 3.5.1 Table 1 and report form p. 5-7): 3 mL now VTBI 3 mL (Ansur 2 mL), 5 mL VTBI 5 mL (Ansur 3 mL), 10 mL VTBI 10 mL (Ansur 5 mL), limits ±1.8 % as in the form, in mL (Ansur ±2 % or ±1 % in g); 1 mL and 2 mL sizes added. Changed from Ansur: occlusion pressure 525 mmHg level at 50 mL/h, 400–650 mmHg for 2 to 50 mL, and 975 mmHg level, 475–1475 mmHg for 1 mL (Table 2, p. 3-12; Ansur had 400–650 for 3 to 50 mL only; “50mlL/h” typo fixed). Changed from Ansur: power-on, functional and visual checks rewritten from 5.5 and 5.6.1 (date and time, gripper abnormal, Wi-Fi, auto-loading added); calibrations are only needed if a test fails; the maintenance passwords were removed. Kept as in Ansur, differs from the manual (for Jonathan to confirm): earth leakage 5000/10000 µA (the manual’s report form lists 347 µA normal and 694 µA single fault, values for its ESA620 set-up, not AS/NZS 3551 limits). Kept as in Ansur (for Jonathan to confirm): insulation is mains to non-earthed accessible part only, with no mains to PE.

steps.title: Visual Inspection
steps.instructions: Service manual 5.5.1 and the maintenance test report (pages 5-2 and 5-5).

items: The parts of the machine are complete, without physical damage, and the enclosure, LCD and buttons have no obvious damage
There is no abnormal noise when the machine is shaken
The power interface has no rust, no foreign matter and no trace of ablation
The power cord is not damaged, and the plug connects tightly to the pump
The fastening clamp is complete without cracks, and the pump can be fixed independently on the infusion stand
The multi-function connector and USB interface are undamaged and free of drug residue, and the USB protection cap is present
The safety label and nameplate are clear and undamaged
Connected to AC power: the AC power indicator and the battery indicator are on
At power-on the speaker and the buzzer both sound (service manual 5.5.2: speaker two beeps, buzzer three beeps) and can be heard
During power-on the red and yellow alarm lamps flash in sequence
After power-on the LCD is normal and the Install Syringe wizard screen is displayed
After power-on the push-pull box extends quickly to the farthest end without abnormal noise, and pressing the door button opens the door automatically
There is no alarm during the power-on test operation
Battery: remove the AC power cord; the pump keeps working normally and shows Battery in Use. Reconnect the power cord

steps.title: Mains voltage
steps.instructions: Plug the ESA612 into the mains supply you are testing from.

steps.title: Protective earth resistance
steps.instructions: Connect the device’s mains lead to the ESA612 equipment outlet. Clip the red test lead to an exposed earthed metal part (such as the pole clamp or a metal screw), or the equipotential point if fitted.

steps.title: Insulation: mains to non-earth accessible conductive part
steps.instructions: Connect the device’s mains lead to the ESA612 equipment outlet and switch the device on. Don’t touch the device during the test.

steps.title: Enclosure leakage
steps.instructions: Connect the device’s mains lead to the ESA612 equipment outlet. Clip the red test lead to an unearthed part of the enclosure.

steps.title: Earth leakage
steps.instructions: Connect the device’s mains lead to the ESA612 equipment outlet. The device will be switched on and off between conditions.

steps.title: Functional Tests
steps.instructions: Service manual 5.6.1 (pages 5-3 and 5-4). Use a syringe, extension tube and test water or saline.

items: The system date and time are consistent with the local real time
Each button rebounds normally and the pump gives the corresponding response, with no crash on any key
Auto-loading: opening the fastening clamp makes the push-pull box extend to the distal position; after the syringe is installed, closing the clamp makes it retract and close the gripper
After a syringe is installed, its brand and specification appear in the list of brands
Gripper abnormal check: close the gripper by hand while the push-pull box extends or retracts, and open it by hand during infusion. The pump gives an abnormal gripper alarm and stops
Normal infusion: install the syringe, set the parameters and press Start. The pump starts normally and the running icon, rate, total and pressure are displayed correctly
Sound and light alarms: trigger a high-priority and a low-priority alarm. The sound and light are normal at both priorities, the volume control works and the alarm mute works
Occlusion alarm: run at 100 mL/h and create an occlusion (upstream and downstream). The pump gives an occlusion alarm within 5 minutes
The alarm and operation are recorded in the history
Touchscreen: the LCD is not blurred or garbled, and the touchscreen responds normally throughout the checks above
Wi-Fi (if fitted): the pump connects to a Wi-Fi hotspot

steps.title: Performance Test
steps.instructions:
Service manual 3.4 and 3.5 (pages 3-3 to 3-12; accuracy and occlusion pressure are due every two years and after a repair). Use the customer's syringes and an extension tube, test water and an electronic balance with enough resolution for the small volumes (the manual does not give one; the Ansur text said 0.1 g, which is too coarse for 1 to 3 mL). 1 g of water = 1 mL.
Accuracy test: draw water slowly, remove all bubbles, and make sure the plunger sits on the full-size scale line before the syringe is installed. Weigh the beaker, run the VTBI at the rate below with the extension tube in the beaker, then weigh again. Confirm the pump's own time matches your timing.
Occlusion pressure test: connect the extension tube to a peak-reading pressure gauge or infusion analyser (peak mode), level with the pump. Run at 50 mL/h at the 525 mmHg occlusion level (975 mmHg for the 1 mL syringe), occlude with the three-way tap and read the peak pressure when the occlusion alarm sounds.
Mark a syringe size N/A if the bench does not use it (1 mL is an optional size).
If a test fails, calibrate to that syringe (service manual 3.4.1 accuracy; 3.4.2 pressure at about 300 and 900 mmHg; Menu > Manufacturer Maintenance > System Calibration; the maintenance passwords are in the service manual) and repeat the test.

items: Accuracy calibration (only if the accuracy test failed): completed successfully, then the test repeated and passed. N/A if not needed
Pressure calibration (only if the occlusion pressure test failed): completed successfully, then the test repeated and passed. N/A if not needed

Sensor calibration (only if the syringe empty size was inaccurate or the specification was misidentified; service manual 3.7): empty size, standard 1 and standard 2 completed successfully. N/A if not needed
